posts.title: Overcoming the Classics
posts.subtitle: A short interlude while I focus on my garden.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Summer is here, friends. I’ve returned from a few trips to find my garden overgrown. The maintenance of which has slowed my writing, but that doesn’t bother me as long as I have soil beneath my fingernails. I hope the change in season has been a welcome one for you. Meanwhile, back to the work.

posts.title: Some housekeeping...
posts.subtitle: Hello friends and subscribers, as if there were any need to delineate those two things.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: I have a tendency to tweak projects in my head whenever I am sick, I can’t write, or when I get back from a trip. All three happened this past month, so here we are.

posts.title: A Night in Mendocino
posts.subtitle: At least the cliffs were free.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: To reclaim what would otherwise be lost forever is a noble pursuit.

posts.title: Sailing on the Sea of Slop
posts.subtitle: This wicked sea, made for you and me.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: To drift in the Sea of Slop may be as good as it gets. Every fascination and every distraction is waiting for me. It may be heaven, in a strange way. I need only sit back and use a remote or swipe a finger, but soon even that won’t be necessary. My eyeballs give everything away. Every blink is a new metric, always being optimized. It has become quite easy to enjoy this heavenly sea that is designed just for you and me.

posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Dear Reader,

posts.title: How Nodes Can Fix Broken Networks
posts.subtitle: A mission statement of sorts from a humble node in an exceedingly vast network
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: We are all a part of a number of networks, and this has been true since we were hunting in tribes. It could be your family, your church, your basketball team, your country or your book club. Some may be more important to you than others, but these networks greatly impact our lives. Now, it feels as if our networks are failing. Social media networks, news networks, but a lot of other networks as well. We should try to fix that.

posts.title: My Favorite Content from 2025
posts.subtitle: How one man spent his limited attention span over the pass 12 months
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Happy New Year to each of you! I wanted to start the year with a commitment to write more for this little Substack project. I’m not quite sure what kind of writing it will be, so hopefully you enjoy the experimentation. But first, something familiar, an end-of-year list!

posts.title: Magical Plugs in the Winter
posts.subtitle: An ode to the rare time when technology does right by us
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: I have a complicated relationship with technology, but in one small way, it gets simpler during the holiday season. It’s a time when we seek out latent emotions and little bits of magic that can bring us together and comfort us as the loneliness of winter approaches.

posts.title: Montana and Wyoming Travel Log
posts.subtitle: Tracking the national vibe shift from Jackson to Whitefish
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: This trip took place in June, with this post sitting in my drafts as a reminder of what has been an unproductive writing period. I hope you still enjoy it, because this trip has stuck with me as we head into the fall.

posts.title: How To Tell if Your Content Diet Isn’t Serving You
posts.subtitle: Welcome to the biggest information buffet in history. Don't fill up on the bread.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Every time we open our phones, we make a choice.

posts.title: Mad Men, Self-Actualization and Being Curious About Who You Want to Become
posts.subtitle: Don Draper would have loved Instagram
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Mad Men* recently celebrated the 10th anniversary of its final episode, which is as good a reason as any to re-position it as a central piece of TV culture. It was one of the first “prestige” shows and it won a whole heap of awards, but that’s not why we should keep it around.

posts.title: Bite-Sized Book Reviews: Abundance, Cryptonomicon and Hell's Angels
posts.subtitle: Because books move slower than newspapers in all the best ways
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Reading has done wonders for my mental health to start the year. The more I see my friends drowning in the daily news barrage, the more I have been drawn to books that either contain an escape, a well-formulated thesis, or a deep dive into a subculture. It’s part of my own attempt to reclaim my attention from sources that only wish to commoditize it.

posts.title: How Substack Should Use Algorithms
posts.subtitle: Since it seems to be happening anyway, we should design our feeds differently this time.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Let’s face it, social media algorithms suck. At least they have so far.

posts.title: 14 Conversation Starters for America's Latest Trade War
posts.subtitle: I have grown bored by what I'm seeing online. Let's change the conversation.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Today’s polarized discourse has really ruined my favorite hobby: Starting interesting conversations that are only *tangential* to current events. This habit is useless now, unless I meet a weirdo like me, because once I know how you voted in the last election, I can often predict the way that you want to talk about tariffs, free trade, manufacturing and America’s role in the world. This conversation would all be downstream of the media sources you consume, the perspectives you’ve chosen to avoid, and the talking points your side wants to get out. The problem is, I can read all of that in the news, so why go there?

posts.title: Make 2025 The Year You Reclaim Your Attention
posts.subtitle: Predictions are so last year. Let's instead create a more effective framework for navigating whatever 2025 throws at us.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: If you’re a consumer of online content, you’re seeing a lot of predictions right now. As a casual writer of online content, I have been tempted to add to the pile.

posts.title: Why Culture Has Drifted to the Right
posts.subtitle: The last few years have proved that the left's dominance over culture is in a downtrend, and it's time for everyone to admit it.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Merry Christmas and Happy Holidays to everyone out there! The added time off of work finally gave me a chance to finish this lengthy piece that I had been working on since early November. As always, thanks for reading, and please leave a comment so we can discuss!

posts.title: Billionaire Influence as America's Funhouse Mirror
posts.subtitle: Elon Musk is opening eyes to a problem that long predated him. He simply outperformed the oligarchs of the left.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: The world is moving quite fast right now. Rather than a fully articulated essay, I will be putting out some short-form thoughts that I’m not seeing articulated elsewhere. I have many thoughts on the election, but for the moment, I am more interested in approaching it from alternative angles.

posts.title: 5 Painful Truths About America For The Overly Ideological
posts.subtitle: Let's disappoint the extreme voices that we can't stop hearing from. Shall we?
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Patriotism has become a partisan issue in America. Many on the left would rather shame those who would hang a flag on the 4th of July. And most of the right goes too far in the opposite direction, driving flag-laden pickup trucks on their way to the grocery store. Meanwhile, both camps are increasingly unhappy about where the country is, and unsure about where it is heading.

posts.title: A broadcast from the front: The current state of America's Influence Wars
posts.subtitle: The right has gained ground in tech, while the left makes surprising advancements on music and sports.
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Good evening, America. You have no doubt experienced the culture wars, but as the battles have raged on, I regret to inform you that the conflict has expanded. And what’s up for grabs? The opinions of normal people, who would rather focus on their own lives. However, turning these individuals into rabid, ideological participants is the fuel that keeps the conflict going, until it can result in real-world consequences.

posts.title: The Last American Bagholder
posts.subtitle: Which way to Easy America?
posts.author: Nicholas Souza
posts.excerpt: Nobody ever told him that America was easy. In fact, he grew up among those who felt that America was challenging. Most of these people had already lost a game that he didn’t know he was playing. It was a game with endless possibilities and nobody was there to explain how it worked. His only clues were found in the bitterness and struggle of those who raised him.
